description: In the IES Rebuild Evaluation memo and in multiple chat answers, I characterized Pydantic AI 1.0 as being under the Sustainable Use License (source-available, not OSI-approved) and even recommended a LangGraph prebuilt-agent fallback to avoid the license. Pydantic AI the agent framework is actually MIT-licensed. The Sustainable Use License applies to Pydantic Logfire (the hosted observability product), not to the framework or to the Pydantic validation library.
correction: Pydantic AI, Pydantic, and FastAPI are MIT. There is no licensing cost or commercial trigger to ship Pydantic AI to a client. The SUL only matters if Logfire is adopted as the observability backend, and that is a service subscription, not a code-license obligation. The Pydantic-AI-vs-LangGraph-prebuilt-agent choice is purely a typing-strength tradeoff, not a license tradeoff.
systemic_fix: Remove the SUL/license caveat from the memo's recommendation and concept-replication sections; state Pydantic AI is MIT and the leaf-agent choice is typing-strength only. When asserting a license for any dependency in a client-shipping context, verify against the actual repo LICENSE file rather than recalling it, and flag that legal should confirm before shipping.
